short.q: Describe how to improve a photograph's composition.
short.model: Crop in to remove distractions, place the subject on a third, use leading lines or a frame within a frame, and choose an unusual viewpoint.

short.q: Compare side light with overcast light.
short.model: Side light makes long shadows that emphasise texture and form. Overcast light is soft and even, with low contrast, so colours are clear but texture looks flatter.

short.q: Describe two digital edits and their effects.
short.model: Cropping improves composition; converting to black and white and raising contrast focuses attention on tone and texture.

short.q: How could a student link photography to AO3?
short.model: Research a photographer such as Dorothea Lange or Hockney, make photographs in their style and write what was learned and how it informs the project.
points: own work in style with reflection

short.q: Why use your own photographs rather than only internet images?
short.model: They are first-hand sources showing personal looking and decisions, adding variety for AO1, and avoid copyright problems.
